Presented by ScottyLabs & 

 TARTANHACKS is the largest Hackathon in Pittsburgh! Organized by ScottyLabs, it's a 24-hour hackathon where participants from all over the country create innovative projects. Come on over to hack, learn from our workshops and incredible speakers, and meet other hackers. 

 MOSAIC 

For 24 hours, participants stepped into a world built from fragments, floating tiles, ideas that refract and snap into place.

Nothing arrived whole; everything began as a piece. Teams gathered scattered bits of vision, skill, and code, assembling them into something greater than any single part. Every insight became a tile and every teammate a new color. As the hours passed, the picture sharpened, a Mosaic taking shape.

Entered with fragments. Left with something whole.

title: Travel Fund | Matthew & Margarethe Mashikian Innovation & Entrepreneurship Hub | College of Engineering | University of Connecticut
text:
Travel Fund | Matthew & Margarethe Mashikian Innovation & Entrepreneurship Hub | College of Engineering | University of Connecticut

 E-Mail : engr-ehub@uconn.edu 

# Travel Fund

The eHub’s Travel Fund helps students, postdocs, and researchers attend external pitch competitions to showcase their tech-enabled innovations. The fund provides up to $750 per competition to cover travel, lodging, and registration costs. By supporting attendance at these events, we aim to help innovators refine their pitches, gain exposure, and build connections with investors, mentors, and collaborators.

## Fund Details

- Eligibility: Students, postdocs, and researchers involved in technology-driven innovations.
- Pitch Acceptance Requirement: Applicants must be confirmed to pitch at the event, and proof of acceptance (e.g., confirmation email or letter) is required as part of the application.
- Award Amount: Up to $750 per event.
- Use of Funds: Travel, lodging, registration fees, and other event-related expenses.
- Expectations: Recipients are expected to submit a short report summarizing their experience, key learnings, and outcomes.

## Application Process

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, but must be submitted at least 6 weeks before the event to allow time for review and funding approval. Early submissions are encouraged.

## Contact Us

For questions or more information, email Dr. Leila Daneshmandi: leila.daneshmandi@uconn.edu.

All teams selected as semi-ﬁnalists will have the option to receive coaching from mentors in global health. text:
ATC 2026: The 2026 ACM SIGOPS Annual Technical Conference

## ATC 2026 Student Scholarships and Travel Grants

ATC 2026 offers a limited number of grants to help full-time undergraduate and graduate students attend the conference in Hong Kong. Students may apply whether or not they are presenting work.

Funding is competitive and may cover conference registration and part of reasonable travel and accommodation expenses. Awards may not cover all requested costs.

### Eligibility

Applicants must:

- be enrolled full-time at an accredited institution;
- study computer science, computer engineering, or a related field;
- attend ATC 2026 in person if selected; and
- disclose all confirmed or pending funding for the trip.

Postdoctoral researchers are also eligible.

### Application Materials

Please submit:

- the completed application form;
- a CV of no more than two pages;
- proof of current full-time student status.

Applications will be evaluated based on financial need, relevance to ATC, expected benefit from attending, available institutional support, and contributions to broad participation.
